_comment: Tier-2 for NGSolve linear_elasticity#0: catalog falsification. Existing pitfall 'Use VectorH1(...), NOT H1(mesh, dim=2)' is wrong — both work and give identical solve results to 1e-16. The real distinction is layout: VectorH1 has ndof=42, dim=1 (flat); H1(dim=2) has ndof=21, dim=2 (block). Their total scalar dofs match. Also confirms MatrixValued(H1, symmetric=True) is real and gfu.components returns tuple of ComponentGridFunction. Verified empirically 2026-06-01. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): this is a falsification fixture, so the control applies the catalog's own (mistaken) prescription rather than removing a pathology: T2_MUTATE=1 builds fes_dim as VectorH1(mesh, order=2, dirichlet='left') instead of H1(mesh, order=2, dim=2, dirichlet='left'), so the space under audit is never exercised. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 4 expect_in_output strings; under T2_MUTATE=1 the second space reports h1_dim2_type=VectorH1 with ndof=42/dim=1 instead of ndof=21/dim=2, so it removes 'h1_dim2_type=H1' and additionally trips the forbidden string 'ERROR' via the source's own ok check, and the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
